title: RAW a partial concession leaves a residual discrepancy supporting an explicitly inferred transfer
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_EXECUTED. Galen III.15 first disputes a nourishment explanation, then grants some nourishment for argument while saying the vessel disparity is too large for that explanation. The remaining discrepancy supports an inferred transfer, whose unseen route must not be turned into direct observation.

source.work: Galen, On the Natural Faculties, cached English translation, Book III chapters 14–15
source.owned_unit: Complete chapters III.14–15, from anchor R14 through the final wine/arterial discussion and book end. The whole body unit was reread; no earlier chapter or new source was acquired.
source.locus: III.15, pp321–323: observed pits with unobservable extreme terminations, followed by the relative vessel-size argument and its nourishment objection/concession.
source.source_limit: Historical physiological and teleological claims, not validated anatomy or a modern proof. The cache contains unresolved footnote markers and visible transcription defects; no Greek or critical-edition collation is claimed.

design.working_hypothesis: A written argument can retain a proposed explanation while conceding only part of its force: even granting some nourishment, the author says a residual disparity remains and uses it to infer an additional transfer. The concession changes the argumentative allowance, not the observed anatomy or the asserted amount actually consumed.

connected_relations.premise: The incoming vessel is described as much larger than the outgoing vessel to the lungs.
connected_relations.written_consequence: The author takes this to suggest that not all incoming blood leaves by that outgoing route.

connected_relations.objection: The discrepancy might be accounted for by nourishment of the heart itself.
connected_relations.written_reply: The source first invokes another nourishing vein, then explicitly grants a certain amount for argument and still calls the disparity too great for the explanation.

connected_relations.remaining_claim: The granted alternative does not, in the author's argument, account for the whole disparity.
connected_relations.written_consequence: The author concludes that something is taken into the left ventricle; nearby wording admits that the extreme ends of the supposed communications cannot actually be observed.

design.distinguishing_consequence: A faithful account must distinguish conceding some nourishment for argument from asserting it as a newly observed quantity. It must also distinguish an inferred transfer/communication from a directly observed complete passage. Rejecting all nourishment outright, accepting it as the entire explanation, or reporting the hidden route as seen would produce different claims despite using the same organ and vessel names.
whole_unit_limits: The preceding account includes an asserted vascular-emptying observation and a teleological argument. They are different claimed grounds, not one measured experiment, and no new animal experiment is proposed.
The source gives qualitative size comparisons, not numerical volume, pressure, velocity, conservation measurements or a quantified residual. Do not manufacture a mass-balance proof.
The visibility limitation concerns the extreme terminations of the described pits. Do not replace it with a claim that nothing whatsoever was visible or that hidden routes were directly traced.

The later account retains the two attraction modes, long conduits versus local uptake, intermediate nourishment and the mobile-fluid countercase. This proposal neither replaces nor duplicates those bodily transport claims by assigning new organs.

The author's conclusion may be historically incorrect or logically insufficient by other standards. The candidate is the written concession-and-inference content, not endorsement of the physiological conclusion.

rivals.name: Categorical exclusion
rivals.account: The alternative consumes nothing and is simply impossible.
rivals.difference: This loses the explicitly allowed certain amount in the even-if reply.

rivals.name: Complete alternative explanation
rivals.account: Granting some nourishment explains the entire discrepancy.
rivals.difference: This removes the author's stated residual and the reason offered for the additional transfer.

rivals.name: Directly observed hidden passage
rivals.account: The terminal communication and its transfer were visually traced.
rivals.difference: This upgrades the source's inference despite its explicit limit on what could be seen.

rivals.name: Independent complete argumentative clauses
rivals.account: Full clauses express the premise, concession and conclusion without a reusable constructor.
rivals.difference: This remains source-compatible; future written recurrence would be needed to favor reusable composition.
